evidence: Replay setup: catanatron 3.3 (/home/user/venv_cat33/bin/python), niced, about 15-16 ms per game. Earlier design: T1 1,000 games in 22.7 s and T2+T3 800 games in 18.2 s. This revision: robstats4.py on 600 T1 games in 9.7 s and robstats4b.py on 400 T1 games in 6.6 s.

Offense (earlier design, unchanged): our robber lands on the clear leader's hex 93.3% (T1) / 92.0% (T2+T3) vs Catanatron's 45.5% / 47.5%; we steal from the leader 73.3% / 69.1%; we block 12.4 opponent pips per move vs their 10.8. Our steals take a needed card 47.9%; the best victim on the same hex would give 50.8%.

Defense (earlier design): we are blocked at the start of 37.5% of our turns, and hold no knight in 85% of those. Cards lost per game: 4.67 to blocks and 3.47 to steals (T1), vs 6.16 and 4.46 per Catanatron seat.

Kick rule, checked (T1, 600 games): turns that start blocked while holding a knight end with the knight played in 649 of 651 cases for our bot and 173 of 174 for Catanatron. By raw blocked pips (ours): 1-2 pips 1/1, 3-4 90/91, 5-6 196/196, 7+ 362/363. Only 2 of the 825 events were 1-2 pip blocks, so the KICK_MIN gate is right but rarely matters against bots. Given the robber is still in place, bots kick about 99.7% of the time. The 67% self-play figure also counts robbers moved earlier by other players' 7s and knights.

Block lifetime (T1, 600 games, 9,522 completed placements): mean 4.34 rolls; 5.3% are kicked before the next roll. Realised share E[min(L,t)]/E[L] for t = 1..5: 0.218, 0.390, 0.525, 0.631, 0.713. Geometric 1-(1-1/4.34)^t: 0.230, 0.408, 0.544, 0.649, 0.730. Linear min(1, t/4.34): 0.230, 0.461, 0.691, 0.922, 1.000. The geometric curve is within 0.02; the linear one overstates the kept share by up to 0.29.

Leader dev cards (T1, 600 games, 2,352 of our clear-leader robber decisions): the leader held at least one dev card at 237 (10.1%). 17 of those held a knight, 220 (93%) held only non-knights, and we hit the leader's hex in 210 (89%). Uniform pool dealing in counted mode would deal a knight for about 56% of a single held card, so R1 would spare most of these leaders unless dealt cards are excluded.

Retaliation (T1, 600 games): a player robbed by k, at their next robber move, steals from k 22.7% of the time for Catanatron seats (1,073/4,728; lands on k's hex 37.1%) and 35.6% for ours (1,015/2,853; hex 55.7%), against a uniform 33.3%. Neither population retaliates, so a retaliation term can only matter against humans.

Victim position (T1, 600 games): Catanatron robs the next roller 75.9% of the time (4,810/6,333). Ours are near uniform: 35.3% next roller, 30.1% two seats on, 34.6% previous player. At our robber moves the opponents hold 5.74, 5.24 and 4.74 cards in that order.

Block vs steal (T1, 400 games, 2,566 of our moves): in 22.7% (583) another hex blocked within 2 pips of our choice, still hit the clear leader if our choice did, and offered a victim with at least 2 more cards. Our chosen victim held 5.0 cards on average, against a 6.8-card maximum opponent hand. A steal takes one card whatever the hand size, so this only bounds the opportunity; the relevant gap is P(needed card), 47.3% vs 50.8%.

Block scale: our placements deny 1.50 cards in total to non-placers (T1). In the leaf, the same move removes about 0.55 x 12.4 = 6.8 static points from the victims, roughly 4.5 points per denied card. A card in hand is worth 0.12 plus build progress. So the leaf values blocks several times higher than steals, which is the premise of R1c.

Self-play (earlier design, about 200 s niced): 24% and 27.5% of robber moves hit a knight holder; 67% of those were kicked by that holder vs 5% otherwise; blocked at 44.5% of turn starts, 16% of them with a knight.

Dev evidence (earlier design, T1+T4, 2,000 games): turn starts blocked by >= 3 pips while holding dev cards, with no dev card played that turn. Cards held: 96.5% VP for our bot (7,474 events), 74.5% VP and 25.4% Road Building for Catanatron (2,347 events), 0 knights. The knight exclusion alone explains only part: a held non-knight is 5/11 = 45% VP in the pool, and the rest comes from Year of Plenty, Monopoly and Road Building being played quickly.

Worked R3 example, recomputed ('any knight' likelihood, 2 held cards, pool 14 K / 5 VP / 2 RB / 2 YoP / 2 Mono): prior E[VP] 0.40; after one event 0.72 with lambda 0.1 and h0 0, 0.88 with lambda 0.01, and 0.59 with lambda 0.1 and hoarder prior h0 0.15. The earlier figure of 0.81 was wrong.

Critique's scratch shadow, cited not re-run (critic_robber/shadow*.py; 40 heuristic self-play games; 260 robber/knight decisions): the default hit a knight holder in 59. Persistence alone changed 41 of those 59 and 1 other decision. Insurance alone changed 11 (7 switched from knight-then-roll to roll, none while blocked) and 6 of 260 main-phase first actions of knight holders (including one BUILD_ROAD that became END_TURN). Cost: about 192 evaluations per decision (median 169, p90 323), 6.9 us per leaf batched vs 6.8 us single, about 10 us of Python correction per leaf, so about 1.15x per decision for the naive wrapper.

Statistics: self-play 2,400 paired games give SE about 1.0 pp. With O'Brien-Fleming looks at 800/1,600/2,400 (one-sided alpha 0.025) the z boundaries are 3.71/2.51/1.99, and power is about 31% at +1.5 pp. Proving +1 pp at 80% power needs about 18,800 games. Against Catanatron, 2,000 seeds give SE about 1.3 pp and an MDE of about 3.7 pp; proving +0.5 pp would need about 105,000 seeds, which is shelve territory under the user's rule. The old non-inferiority rule (lower bound > -2 pp) passes a neutral feature only 34% of the time. The new harm screen (FAIL if the upper bound < 0 or the point estimate <= -1.85 pp) false-fails 8% and catches a -3.7 pp harm 92% of the time.

features.name: Zero-game robber shadow and observation-only robber counters (tooling; gates everything else)
features.description:
Two pieces of tooling. Neither changes the bot.

(1) scripts/robber_shadow.py, generalised from scripts/winpaths_shadow.py.
- Plays N games of the default bot in one process.
- At every MOVE_ROBBER choice, every PHASE_ROLL decision of a seat holding a playable knight, and every PHASE_MAIN decision, it re-searches the root twice with the same random.Random(k): once with the default config and once with a candidate.
- The candidate is spec keys plus registry overrides, applied through ParamBot's override scope, using the bot's own model, belief and politics.
- For each decision it records both first actions, a classification (does the default's hex block a would-kick knight holder; did the robber land on the clear leader's hex; blocked pips; was a knight kept while exposed), both process times, and the corrections at the leaves (used to calibrate INS_OFFSET).
- It also screens the queued prior-only campaign rows: t2_block_need0, t2_turns_half2, t2_danger_mult_off, t2_steal_factor_off and t2_rob_break_off.

(2) catanbot/robber_metrics.py RobberCounters, an on_action observer that never uses the RNG. Per seat it counts:
- robber moves, moves onto a would-kick knight holder, moves on the clear leader's hex;
- blocked turn starts with and without a knight;
- cards lost to blocks and to steals;
- knights played, and knights held at END_TURN while exposed;
- Largest Army at the end of the game.

It is wired into CatanbotPlayer.stats, which ablate_catanatron already saves per game as 'adapter' and totals as adapter_cand/adapter_def. It is also wired into tuning.play_paired_game: an always-on on_action composed with count_counters, which adds 'seat_robber' to the result dict. This leaves scripts/ablate.py and scripts/tune_joint.py (the SPSA/factorial agent's files) untouched.
plug_in_points: new scripts/robber_shadow.py (copy of the winpaths_shadow.py pattern; PHASE_ROBBER / PHASE_ROLL / PHASE_MAIN; --cand-keys and --tune NAME=V)
new catanbot/robber_metrics.py (RobberCounters.on_action, to_dict)
catanbot/tuning.py:play_paired_game (L594-630): compose RobberCounters with count_counters and add 'seat_robber' to the returned dict (observation only)

catanbot/bench/catanatron_adapter.py: CatanbotPlayer observe path updates self.stats robber keys (rob_moves, rob_on_knight_holder, rob_on_leader, blocked_turns, blocked_turns_knight, cards_lost_block, cards_lost_steal, knights_played, knights_held_exposed, army_end)
new scripts/pool_paired.py (pool disjoint-seed ablate.py JSON reports; OBF boundaries via catanbot/league/sequential.py)
features.off_switch: Not a bot feature: no tunable, because the bot is unchanged. The counters are observation-only and consume no RNG, and a test proves game results are identical with and without them.
features.cpp_impact: None.
features.cost: Shadow: two extra root searches per covered decision, about 3x the default time on those decisions. 40 games is about 20-30 min on one niced core, and runs only after the proof frees the cores. Counters: under 1% per game.
features.expected_effect: No win-rate effect. It decides which robber ideas get games at all. If 3-5 of the prior-only t2 rows change fewer than 2% of robber decisions, pruning them saves about 1.5-2.5 h of campaign time against value. It also supplies the mechanism metrics that the harm screens and SHELVE readings need.
features.how_to_test: Unit tests, a 2-game smoke run, and one identity run: a shadow with candidate == default must report 0 changed decisions.
tests_to_write: test_robber_counters_do_not_change_games (result hash identical with the counters on or off, 6 games)
test_robber_counters_match_replay_on_fixture (counts on a fixture game equal a hand-computed replay)
features.moderate_fallback: If the one-process shadow is too slow, cover only PHASE_ROBBER and knight PHASE_ROLL decisions (about 10% of decisions) and sample 1 in 5 main-phase decisions.

features.name: Robber persistence leaf correction: blocks on a would-kick knight holder are mostly temporary (R1a)
features.description:
Adds a correction to each blocked player's C++ static value before the softmax. It is active only with SearchConfig.robber_corr=1 and lives in a Python leaf wrapper, so static_value is untouched.

The idea: a block on a player who will kick it at their next turn start (holds a playable knight, and the block is worth at least the knight rule's 3.0 demand-weighted pips) is mostly undone before it costs production. So we restore the share of the leaf's block value that will not happen, taking into account who kicks first and the geometric chance that the block would have ended anyway.

Consequences: our robber stops spending its block on next-to-roll knight holders; the steal still happens and is priced as before. It also forgets less that a block on us is temporary when we hold a knight.

Counted mode and the advisor: seats whose dev cards were dealt by the tracker (passed as a search hint) count as knight holders only through a supplied posterior P(knight) from the card-counting area. Without one they count as 0, the pre-R1 behaviour, so a secret-VP leader is never spared. In full-information games and self-play the knights are known.

Optional RETAL_W (default 0) prices the kicker's next robber landing on us. It is a table-social term (politics rule), and the logs show neither Catanatron nor our bot retaliates, so it stays 0 and is deferred to human testing.
features.formulas:
All values are in static points (10 = 1 VP). The leaf value is softmax((V + C) / 16)[me], where V = C++ static_values(s).

1. Blocked value. h = s.robber, r = its resource. w_r = RESOURCE_DEMAND[r] x sqrt(scarcity_r). pv_i(h) = hex_pips_for_player(s, h, i) x w_r. This equals robber.production_blocked when h is the robber hex, so 0.55 x pv_i(h) is exactly what the leaf removed.

2. Roll order. If s.phase == PHASE_ROLL: c, c+1, ..., c+n-1. Otherwise: c+1, ..., c+n-1, c (mod n). t_k = the number of rolls before k's next turn start.

3. Would-kick set. KK = {k : pv_k(h) >= KICK_MIN (3.0) and q_k > 0}, where q_k = 1 if dev_cards[K] + dev_cards_new[K] >= 1 and k's cards are known (full information, or k = me). For a dealt seat, q_k = the supplied P(knight), else 0. kappa_k = KICK_LAMBDA (0.95) x q_k.

4. First kicker. Order KK by t_k. P1_k = kappa_k x product over k' in KK with t_k' < t_k of (1 - kappa_k').

5. Restore. a = 1 - 1/R_REF, with R_REF = 4.34 rolls (measured). rho = sum over k in KK of P1_k x a^t_k. (Geometric lifetime: a kick after t rolls avoids the share a^t of the block's loss.)

6. C_i^pers = PERSIST_W x 0.55 x pv_i(h) x rho for every i with pv_i(h) > 0, including us.

7. Optional retaliation: C_me^retal = -RETAL_W x sum over k != me of P1_k x a^t_k x P_tgt_k(me) x 0.55 x HIT_SHARE (0.9) x max over h' != h of pv_me(h'). P_tgt is as in robber.knight_insurance.

Examples (w about 1):
- next roller (t=0) with a knight and a 5-pip settlement: rho = 0.95, C = 2.61 of the 2.75 block;
- the same player third to roll (t=2): rho = 0.95 x 0.77^2 = 0.56, C = 1.55;
- a 2-pip block on a knight holder: rho = 0.

Fast path: evaluate the batch with heuristic_evaluate first. Recompute (single-state static_values, then a Python softmax) only the leaves with some C_i != 0. When every C_i is 0 the output is bit-identical to the base.
plug_in_points: new catanbot/robber_eval.py: RobberContext (per-search; per-hex pv tables keyed on every seat's building sets, winpaths._osig pattern; P1/rho are computed per leaf and never cached), RobberEvaluator(base, ctx) with the fast path; setup and game-over leaves pass through; register_tunables(registry)

catanbot/search.py: SearchConfig.robber_corr: int = 0. Searcher.search builds one self._leaf_ev next to self._paths (L281) and uses it at the three 'ev = self.evaluator if self._paths is None else self._paths' sites (_eval L367, the counter ranking L496, political options L570). The native _future_values gate (L854) also requires robber_corr == 0. robber_corr=1 together with paths=1 raises a clear error until a shared corrections hook exists.
catanbot/tuning.py: one line at the end, 'from .robber_eval import register_tunables as _register_robber; _register_robber(TUNABLES)', as for winpaths at L821
catanbot/selfplay.py make_bot: spec key robber_corr (spec_key == attr, as in the paths precedent asserted by tests/test_winpaths.py L793)

dealt-seat hint: catanbot/bench/catanatron_adapter.py _decide_counted passes the tracker's dealt seats (and later P(knight) from the card-counting posterior) as a per-decision search hint; empty in full-information games and self-play
NOT touched: robber.steal_exposure_fast (C++-mirrored), counting.expected_hidden_vp (C++-mirrored), scripts/ablate.py, scripts/tune_joint.py
features.off_switch:
search.robber_corr: kind search, int, default 0 (spec key robber_corr). With 0 the wrapper is never built, so the default is byte-identical. Module weights, all kind weight with requires_search and NOT needs_python_evaluator, read only when robber_corr=1:
- robber_eval.PERSIST_W = 1.0
- KICK_LAMBDA = 0.95
- KICK_MIN = 3.0
- R_REF = 4.34
- RETAL_W = 0.0
- PLACEBO = 0 (1 rotates the corrections to the next seat as a control arm, the winpaths precedent)
robber_corr=1 alone is persistence-only, because INSURANCE_W and BLOCK_DUR_W default to 0.
features.cpp_impact:
None. static_value (Python and C++) and every C++-mirrored helper are untouched. The wrapper calls the C++ heuristic_evaluate and static_values and adds the correction in Python, so it needs neither needs_python_evaluator (about 3x slower games) nor a C++ port. The native depth >= 2 lookahead (cpp/search.cpp) cannot see the term, so depth >= 2 with robber_corr=1 takes the Python future-values path, as paths=1 does.

Recommendation: do not port during screening. Port only if R1a is adopted AND depth 2 becomes the default. The port would add a RobberCorr parameter struct to heuristic_evaluate/future_values plus a parity test.
features.cost: Measured by the critique: about 192 evaluations per decision, 6.9 us per batched leaf, about 10 us of Python correction per corrected leaf. With the fast path only leaves whose robber hex blocks a would-kick holder are recomputed (an estimated 5-15% of leaves), so about 1.02-1.1x ms per decision. The per-search context build is about 0.1-0.3 ms. The shadow gate caps it at 1.2x mean and 1.5x p95.
features.expected_effect:
Decisions changed (the critique's shadow on the old linear formula): 41 of 59 robber decisions that hit a knight holder, about 16% of robber/knight decisions and about 1 per seat-game in self-play. Against Catanatron only about 2% of our moves hit a knight holder, so it is nearly inert there.

The mechanism is modest: the steal still happens, and the forced knight play moves the victim toward Largest Army. The gain is about 1 card of wasted block per seat-game, shared with the other opponents.

Realistic win effect: +0.5 to +1.5 pp in self-play, against a final OBF boundary of about 2.0 pp, so the pre-registered expectation is SHELVE (power about 31% at +1.5 pp). Against Catanatron: about 0.
features.how_to_test:
Step 0, zero-game shadow: scripts/robber_shadow.py --games 40 --cand-keys robber_corr=1. Gates:
- G1: at least 30% of default robber/knight decisions whose hex blocks a would-kick knight holder with t <= 1 change;
- G2: at most 3% of other robber/knight decisions change;
- G3: at most 1% of main-phase first actions change;
- G4: ms ratio at most 1.2 mean and 1.5 p95.
Failing G1 or G4 puts the feature on ice and moves to the fallback.

Step 1, self-play, persistence only (no hoarding asymmetry, so no 2v2 teammate artifact), 3 x 800 paired 4-player games on disjoint seeds:
  nice -n 10 python3 scripts/ablate.py --tunable search.robber_corr --values 1 --base-spec search:depth=1,beam=4,expand=8,evaluator=heuristic --games 800 --players 4 --seed 21 --workers 3 --json runs/robcorr_sp_s21.json
then seeds 22 and 23, about 0.75 h each at 3 workers. Pool with scripts/pool_paired.py.

Decision rules:
- ADOPT if the win-rate z or the paired VP-difference z crosses its OBF boundary (alpha split 0.0125 one-sided each; about 3.96 / 2.77 / 2.27) and the other point estimate is >= 0.
- Futility: stop after 1,600 games if the pooled win-rate estimate is <= 0; that is a REJECT.
- At 2,400 games: REJECT if the upper 95% bound is < +1 pp; otherwise SHELVE.

Mechanism readout from seat_robber (primary for reading a SHELVE):
- candidate robber moves onto would-kick holders at <= 50% of the default seats' rate;
- candidate-on-candidate hit share reported against the baseline;
- guards: Largest Army share at the end down no more than 3 pp; knights played per game within ±0.3.

Step 2, only if Step 1 ADOPTs or its pooled estimate is >= +1.5 pp: a harm screen against Catanatron value, 2,000 paired seeds (about 2 h):
  nice -n 10 /home/user/venv_cat33/bin/python scripts/ablate_catanatron.py --cand-spec search:depth=1,beam=4,expand=8,evaluator=heuristic,robber_corr=1 --def-spec search:depth=1,beam=4,expand=8,evaluator=heuristic --opponent value --seeds 2000 --workers 3 --out runs/robcorr_value.jsonl
FAIL if the 95% upper bound is < 0 or the point estimate is <= -1.85 pp (8% false-fail, 92% power at -3.7 pp); otherwise PASS. Then the league gate.

This replaces the planned KNIGHT_VALUE x EXPOSURE_WEIGHT factorial (see robber.knight_insurance).
tests_to_write: test_robber_corr_off_byte_identical (fresh-interpreter hash over 6 games and 30 searches, including ParamBots with robber_eval weights overridden while robber_corr=0; copies test_default_unchanged_six_games_and_thirty_searches)
test_robber_corr_zero_weights_action_identical (robber_corr=1 with PERSIST_W=0: the fast path returns the base values bit for bit)
test_earliest_kicker_order (two holders: the earlier roller dominates, and the restore is smaller when only the later roller holds a knight)
test_dealt_seat_knights_not_trusted (hint marks a seat as dealt: q = 0 unless a posterior is supplied)
test_cache_cold_vs_warm_identical (opponent builds inside the search via respond_lookahead=1; same corrections cold and warm)
test_registry_robber_eval (verify_registry passes; spec_key == attr; not needs_python_evaluator; test_ablate::test_cpp_static_value_constants_are_flagged still passes)
features.moderate_fallback: A candidate filter with no evaluator change. In Searcher._candidates, drop MOVE_ROBBER/PLAY_KNIGHT candidates whose only blocked opponents are next-to-roll would-kick knight holders, when an alternative within 1 static point exists. Prior tweaks are not a fallback, because priors are inert at depth 1. The old knight-after-roll rule is removed: a pre-roll knight followed by a 7 still steals and still counts toward Largest Army.

features.name: Blocked-no-play likelihood for held dev cards: secret-VP leader and knight holders (R3, handed to the card-counting area)
features.description:
When a player starts their turn as the main robber victim while holding older dev cards and plays none, a held knight is unlikely: bots kick about 99.7% of the time. This is the user's rule (knights get used to kick the robber; cards held a long time are likely VP) as a likelihood event.

It belongs in the card-counting area's general dev-type posterior (held age, Year of Plenty and Road Building played fast, Monopoly depending on the bank), which should absorb it. This area supplies:
- the event definition;
- the likelihood;
- the exact sampler;
- the plumbing fix;
- the consumers: R1a/R1b's P(knight) for dealt seats, dealt VP cards so the softmax and robber see a secret leader, and advice text.

Fixes from the critiques:
- Exact per-player posterior dealing replaces joint rejection. Joint rejection often exhausted the 20 attempts and kept a knight deal.
- A mixture likelihood with a hoarder prior and a capped count, so correlated non-plays by humans do not become certainty.
- An event counts only when j is the main victim.
- Fit on opponent seats only (the 96.5% figure is our own policy).
- The offline gain is measured against a held-age/per-type hazard baseline, not against uniform dealing.
- Blocker fixed: determinization now runs inside the candidate's override scope, so the ablate_catanatron candidate arm really differs.
plug_in_points: catanbot/public_belief.py (card-counting area): evidence counters updated in observe regardless of the flag (no RNG, so default determinizations are unchanged); an exact-posterior branch in _deal_devs (L255) entered only when KNIGHT_EVIDENCE=1; dev_marginals(j)
catanbot/bench/public_info.py: PublicInfoTracker snapshots the robber hex and blocked values at j's first action and raises the event at END_TURN
catanbot/colonist_log.py: the same event for the advisor

catanbot/agents/param_bot.py: a public scope() context manager wrapping _enter/_exit; catanbot/bench/catanatron_adapter.py wraps tracker.determinize in 'with scope(self.bot)', so belief-layer tunables reach the candidate arm
consumer: robber_eval gets P(knight) for dealt seats through the search hint (R1a/R1b)
NOT touched: counting.expected_hidden_vp (C++-mirrored at cpp L499; the advisor uses determinizations instead)
features.cpp_impact: None. This is the belief layer, Python only. The hook into the C++-mirrored expected_hidden_vp is dropped, so no public-view parity case is needed.
features.cost: Negligible. Enumerating at most 35 multisets per evidence player per determinization, K=4 determinizations per decision.
features.expected_effect:
It acts only in counted mode and in the advisor.
- Against Catanatron in counted mode the event fires about 1.2 times per game on their seats, and a hidden-VP leader appears at 1-5% of our robber decisions.
- The leader holds dev cards at 10.1% of our clear-leader robber decisions, and 93% of those hold no knight. Without R3 or an equivalent posterior, R1 must ignore dealt knights entirely.
- Game effect against bots: +0 to +1 pp, below the MDE.
- Main value: calibrated secret-VP and knight odds for Colonist play against humans, and a safe P(knight) for R1 in counted mode.
features.how_to_test:
Step 1, zero games, about 0.3 h CPU (the card-counting area's replay harness). Replay the 5,000 archived proof games through PublicInfoTracker's counted view, opponent (Catanatron) seats only. At every opponent turn start, predict P(holds >= 1 VP), E[VP] and P(holds >= 1 knight) under three models:
- (a) uniform pool dealing;
- (b) the held-age/per-type hazard baseline;
- (c) (b) plus the R3 event.
Fit lambda and h0 on T1+T4 and evaluate on T2, T3, T5 and T6. Gate: (c) must cut log-loss for P(knight) and MAE of E[VP] by at least 5% relative to (b) on held-out data, with deciles calibrated within ±5 pp; otherwise REJECT R3 as a separate term.

Step 2, only if Step 1 passes: a counted-mode harm screen against value, 2,000 paired seeds (about 2 h at 3 workers):
  --info counted --cand-spec <default>,tune=public_belief.KNIGHT_EVIDENCE:1
Preconditions: the integration test (below) passes, and the run reports more than 0 non-identical pairs.
FAIL if the 95% upper bound is < 0 or the point estimate is <= -1.85 pp.

Adoption for counted mode and the advisor: the offline gain plus a PASS (see open questions). Humans are validated through the advisor.
tests_to_write: test_candidate_arm_first_determinization_differs (integration: ParamBot scope around determinize; the fixture log contains a blocked-no-play event)
features.moderate_fallback: Use the evidence only for P(holds a knight): it feeds R1's q for dealt seats and the advice text, and VP dealing stays unchanged. If even that fails calibration, R1 keeps q = 0 for dealt seats permanently.

features.name: Centred knight-insurance leaf correction with opponent-habit targeting (R1b; an SPSA knob, no standalone A/B)
features.description:
A held knight nearly cancels a block: the victim lost 0.18 cards instead of 1.34 and kicked 89% of the time. So a knight should be worth more to a player likely to be robbed soon.

Redesigned after the critiques:
- The target model uses the opponent model's observed robber victims (profile.robbed with a trust ramp) and a population prior built from threat and blockable pips. It never uses hand size, so holding more cards cannot raise a knight holder's value (this removes the perverse incentive of the old steal-exposure key).
- Spare knights count: a blocked player with 2 or more knights keeps insurance after kicking.
- The term is centred on its calibrated mean, INS_OFFSET. It moves knight value from unexposed to exposed positions without raising the average, which separates it from the KNIGHT_VALUE rows and the flat 0.7.
- INSURANCE_W is the horizon multiplier (rounds of cover) and gets tuned, not fixed at 1.
- Dealt seats in counted mode get no insurance unless the card-counting area supplies a posterior.

It lives in the same wrapper as R1a.

Why no standalone test: the expected win effect is about +0.3 to +0.8 pp, mostly against Catanatron (they hit us about 25% of rounds). Proving +0.5 pp would take about 105,000 seeds, which the user's rule shelves. So after the shadow gate it goes to the SPSA robber group as a knob; the SPSA owner is asked, not edited.
features.formulas:
For each player i and each opponent j of i (all in static points):

1. Blockable pips. bp_x = max over h' != robber of pv_x(h').

2. Prior target. prior_j(i) = TGT_LEAD (0.5) x 1[i = argmax over x != j of threat(x)] + (1 - TGT_LEAD) x bp_i / sum over x != j of bp_x.

3. Observed habit, when the opponent model is used. share_j(i) = robbed_j[i] / sum of robbed_j; trust tau_j = min(1, sum of robbed_j / 3). P_tgt_j(i) = (1 - tau_j) x prior_j(i) + tau_j x share_j(i).

4. Robber move chance per turn. p_rob_j = 1/6 + (5/6) x q_j x KNIGHT_OFF (0.5), with q_j as in R1a. This reimplements the steal_exposure_fast convention in robber_eval.py without touching that function.

5. Hit chance per round. P_hit_i = 1 - product over j != i of (1 - p_rob_j x P_tgt_j(i)).

6. Exposure. D_i = HIT_SHARE (0.9; Catanatron hit 7.7 of our 8.5 max pips) x bp_i.

7. Insured. K_spare_i = K_i - 1[i in the would-kick set of the current robber hex]. Player i is insured if K_spare_i >= 1 and i's cards are known.

8. Correction. C_i^ins = INSURANCE_W x 0.55 x INS_AVERT (0.85) x (D_i x P_hit_i - INS_OFFSET) if insured, else 0. Only one knight counts.

Calibration: INS_OFFSET = the mean of D x P_hit over insured players at the shadow's leaves (about 2.0 expected).

Scale per unit INSURANCE_W with INS_OFFSET 2.0:
- exposed leader, 8.5-pip best hex (D 7.65), P_hit 0.35: +0.32;
- quiet holder, D 5, P_hit 0.1: -0.70.
SPSA range for INSURANCE_W: 0 to 3.
plug_in_points: catanbot/robber_eval.py: RobberContext precomputes bp_x per leaf from the building-keyed pv tables; P_tgt reads self.model.profile_of(...).robbed when cfg.use_opponent_model; robbed_probability(...) is a new helper (steal_exposure_fast untouched)
same Searcher._leaf_ev wiring as R1a (no additional search.py change)
request to the tune_joint owner (no edit here): add robber_eval.INSURANCE_W (0-3) to GROUPS['robber'] with search:...,robber_corr=1 in the SPSA base spec
features.cpp_impact: None, for the same reasons as R1a: the same wrapper, and neither steal_exposure_fast nor static_value changes. It is not in the native depth >= 2 lookahead.
features.cost: The correction is nonzero at every leaf with an insured player, so more leaves take the recompute path: about 1.1-1.3x ms per decision (about 10 us of Python per corrected leaf at about 192 leaves per decision). The shadow gate caps it at 1.3x mean.
features.expected_effect:
In the critique's shadow (old uncentred formula), 11 of 260 robber/knight decisions changed (7 of them knight-then-roll became roll) and 6 of 260 main-phase decisions of knight holders.

Expected mechanism: we hold a knight more often when exposed. Blocks that hit us while we hold a knight rise from about 15% to about 20-25%, saving about 0.3-0.6 cards per game against Catanatron.

Win effect: about +0.3 to +0.8 pp, far below every MDE in the budget. It is useful only through joint tuning.
tests_to_write: test_insurance_independent_of_hand_size (adding cards never raises a knight holder's C_ins)
features.moderate_fallback: A candidate filter: drop an offensive PLAY_KNIGHT when we hold exactly one knight, we are not blocked, our P_hit is above TGT threshold 0.3, and the play neither takes nor defends Largest Army nor hits a player who can win this round. Screen it in the shadow; it would also go to SPSA or be shelved.

features.name: Block-duration discount for every blocked player (R1c; a shadow plus an SPSA knob)
features.description:
The leaf treats every block as permanent production loss. It costs the victim 0.55 x pv, about 6.8 static points summed over victims for our average move. Yet a placement lasts 4.34 rolls and denies only 1.50 cards in total, while a stolen card is worth 0.12 plus build progress to each side.

So in the final choice, blocking is overweighted relative to the steal (and to what the steal takes), and offensive knights look better than they are. BLOCK_DUR_W restores a fixed share of every block's leaf value in the same wrapper. It composes with R1a: the total restore is rho + BLOCK_DUR_W x (1 - rho).

The direction of the effect on win rate is uncertain. The 0.55/0.25 split is a C++-mirrored constant that implicitly sets the block's weight, and the bot's strength was measured with it. So this is a joint-tuning knob, not an A/B candidate.
features.formulas:
For each i with pv_i(h) > 0: C_i^dur = BLOCK_DUR_W x 0.55 x pv_i(h) x (1 - rho_i), where rho_i is R1a's restore (0 when PERSIST_W=0). SPSA candidates are 0.25 and 0.5, range 0 to 0.8. Above about 0.8 the block barely matters and robber choice becomes steal-driven.

Zero-game readout: the share of changed robber/knight decisions. Among changed robber decisions, report the change in P(needed card from the chosen victim) (baseline 47.3%, best on the same hex 50.8%), in blocked leader pips, and in offensive knights per game.
plug_in_points: catanbot/robber_eval.py: one extra term in RobberEvaluator (same fast path)
request to the tune_joint owner: robber_eval.BLOCK_DUR_W (0-0.8) in GROUPS['robber'] if the shadow shows at least 2% of robber/knight decisions change
features.off_switch: robber_eval.BLOCK_DUR_W: kind weight, requires_search, not needs_python_evaluator, default 0.0. Read only when search.robber_corr=1.
features.cpp_impact: None (same wrapper). The equivalent change inside static_value would alter the C++-mirrored 0.55/0.25 split; the wrapper avoids that.
features.cost: Nonzero at every leaf where the robber blocks anyone (most leaves), so most leaves take the recompute path: about 1.15-1.3x ms per decision, as the critique measured for the naive wrapper.
features.expected_effect: Likely changes 5-15% of robber/knight decisions (fewer marginal offensive knights, victims chosen more by need). Win effect of uncertain sign, about ±1 pp. Its value is as a joint-tuning dimension together with INSURANCE_W and the existing EXPOSURE_WEIGHT.
features.how_to_test:
Shadow: scripts/robber_shadow.py --cand-keys robber_corr=1 --tune robber_eval.PERSIST_W=0,robber_eval.BLOCK_DUR_W=0.5 over 40 games.
- If fewer than 2% of robber/knight decisions change, drop it.
- Otherwise hand it to the SPSA robber group (request to the owner); adoption goes through SPSA plus the league gate.
No standalone A/B.
features.moderate_fallback: Apply the discount only to the steal-versus-block trade-off inside the robber decision: C^dur only at leaves whose last action was MOVE_ROBBER or PLAY_KNIGHT, so builds and dev buys are unaffected.

risks: Effect sizes. Against Catanatron every robber refinement is below the detectable effect at 2,000 seeds (about 3.7 pp; about 0.2 VP). In self-play the realistic gain from persistence (+0.5 to +1.5 pp) sits below the final OBF boundary (about 2.0 pp). Expect SHELVE; the counters and the shadow make a SHELVE informative ('works but small' vs 'does not act').

Counted mode and the advisor. Dealt dev cards look like knights about 56% of the time, and the leader holds unknown dev cards at 10% of our clear-leader robber decisions (93% of them non-knights). R1a/R1b therefore ignore dealt knights (q = 0) until the card-counting area supplies a posterior. When it does, a guard applies: with robber_corr=1 in counted mode, the share of our robber moves on a clear leader who holds unknown dev cards must not fall by more than 3 pp.

Teammate artifact in 2v2 self-play: insurance makes candidate seats hold knights, so candidates may spare each other. That is why the self-play A/B is persistence-only (symmetric knight holding), and insurance goes to SPSA and 1v3 settings.

Softmax coupling: a correction on one seat shifts every share. The terms are in static points, calibrated from the logs (0.55 x pv, R_REF 4.34, KICK_LAMBDA 0.95), and the shadow checks that non-robber decisions change by at most 1%.

The forced-knight quirk: static_value scores a forced knight play as -0.25 for the victim (0.7 held becomes 0.45 played) while the victim actually gains Largest Army progress. Persistence reduces how often we force such plays, but the quirk sits in the C++-mirrored static_value and stays out of scope.

Wrapper stacking: winpaths.PathsEvaluator's kind == 'other' branch evaluates base, corrected and uncorrected, about 3x per leaf. robber_corr + paths is refused until one shared corrections hook (paths, robber, ports) is agreed with those owners.

Code-fingerprint churn: any catanbot/*.py change alters ablate_catanatron's code fingerprint (code_files/code_fingerprint L234-259), so earlier default-arm games cannot be reused or paired. Land all flag-off code for this area in one commit, between campaign batches and before any of its runs.

File ownership: public_belief.py, public_info.py, colonist_log.py and the determinize scope in catanatron_adapter.py belong to the card-counting area (R3 is handed over). tuning.py is shared: one registration line plus the observation-only counters. ablate.py and tune_joint.py are not edited; the SPSA changes are requests.

Calibration populations: KICK_LAMBDA, the R3 lambda and h0, and TGT_LEAD are fitted on bots, which kick about 99.7% of the time and never hoard. Humans differ, so the defaults are conservative (0.95, 0.1 with h0 0.15, 0.5) and are validated through the advisor.
The earlier prior-vs-actual agreement figures (67.1% / 74.5%) were computed without the politics target weights, so they are approximate. The shadow replaces them with exact decision-level counts.
All game runs wait until the pre-registered proof (T7-T11) frees the cores. The proof runs from /home/user/proof_snapshot2, so repository edits cannot contaminate it.

open_questions: Adoption evidence (partial disagreement with critique 1). Critique 1 wants the mechanism outcomes to be the primary evidence for adoption, together with 'not significantly worse'. I kept win rate and paired VP difference as co-primaries (alpha split, OBF). The mechanism outcomes gate further spending and tell a 'works but small' SHELVE from a 'does not act' one, but they cannot turn a SHELVE into an ADOPT. The user's rule shelves anything that needs tens of thousands of games to prove, and a mechanism shift is not a win. Does the user want mechanism-plus-harm-screen adoption for belief-quality or insurance-type features, or should they be SHELVED?

The queued prior-only t2 rows (disagreement with critique 1). Critique 1 says run t2_block_need0, t2_turns_half2, t2_danger_mult_off and t2_steal_factor_off as planned and use their REJECTs to prune the SPSA group. I follow critique 2 instead: shadow them first, adding t2_rob_break_off, and run only rows that change at least 2% of robber decisions. Confirming inertness with 1,000 seeds each costs about 1.5-2.5 h, while the shadow costs minutes, and the pilot already found 15-19 of 20 identical games. May the campaign skip the rows the shadow shows are inert?

Insurance testing (partial disagreement with critique 2). Critique 2 suggests testing insurance 1-vs-3 against Catanatron. The expected +0.3 to +0.8 pp would need about 10^5 seeds, so by the user's rule I made it an SPSA knob gated by the shadow. Critique 2's 'robber package' bundle (persistence + R2 + knight-after-roll) is also not adopted: R2 is not built, knight-after-roll rests on a wrong premise (critique 1), and persistence acts in self-play while insurance acts mostly against Catanatron, so bundling does not add power in either population. The fix is to run determinize inside ParamBot's override scope, which also repairs every future belief-layer tunable in the card-counting area. The adapter option remains the alternative if that owner prefers it.

Retaliation (RETAL_W). This is a politics/table-social term, so it would normally get one screen. The logs show neither bot population retaliates: Catanatron steals from its last robber 22.7% of the time and we do 35.6%, against a uniform 33%. A bot screen can therefore detect nothing. May it be declared INCONCLUSIVE without a screen and deferred straight to human testing?

critique_verdicts.lens: Catan strategy and correctness: rules (knight before the roll, one dev card per turn, dev cards not playable the turn they are bought, a random single-card steal, hidden VP cards), how strong human players use the robber, and whether the formulas' magnitudes are sane on the static-value scale (10 points = 1 VP). I checked the claims against catanbot/heuristic.py, robber.py, danger.py, search.py, public_belief.py, opponent_model.py, winpaths.py, tuning.py, the campaign plan and docs/ABLATIONS.md.
critique_verdicts.verdict:
The diagnosis is sound. Offence is near its ceiling, defence is where the cards go, need-aware blocking only orders moves at depth 1, and a held knight nearly cancels a block. Putting the fix in a PathsEvaluator-style wrapper rather than in the C++-mirrored static_value is the right architecture. The measured wrapper cost of about 1.25x makes the cost claim plausible, and neither needs_python_evaluator nor a C++ port is required.

R1 (knight persistence and insurance) is the one feature worth building, but not as specified:
- Its insurance term uses a target model the design's own data refute against Catanatron, which is the only population in Stage C.
- In counted and Colonist mode, its knight estimate would make the bot spare secret-VP leaders, the opposite of the user's rule.
- Its kick probability ignores block size and uses a linear keep curve.
- It ignores where the kicked robber lands (retaliation).
- Its test plan is under-powered: the non-inferiority rule fails a neutral feature about two thirds of the time, and the realistic self-play effect is below the detectable effect, so mechanism outcomes should be the primary evidence.

R3 is strategically right (knights get used to kick the robber), but the rejection sampling would silently drop the evidence, the likelihood is overconfident for humans, and it explains only part of the measured VP skew. It should become one likelihood term in the card-counting area's dev posterior.

R2 has a normalisation bug that shrinks almost every block, and its expected ±1 pp effect falls under the user's shelve rule. Do not build it; use the cheap existing t2 screens to prune the SPSA robber group instead.

R4 is worth nothing and wrongly claims that the swap repair conserves totals. Drop it.

Recommended order: fix R1 as above and screen it (persistence-only as the moderate fallback), fold R3 into card counting, and add the zero-game steal-versus-block valuation check as the next candidate in this area.

critique_verdicts.lens: Engineering and testability: whether the default stays byte-identical, whether the plug-in points exist in the code, whether C++ parity and the search's cost budget hold, whether the effects can be detected within the game budgets, whether the tests cover it, and whether it collides with files other areas are changing. I checked the claims against the code: search.py, heuristic.py, robber.py, winpaths.py, accel.py, tuning.py, agents/param_bot.py, public_belief.py, catanatron_adapter.py, scripts/ablate*.py, tune_joint.py, league/sequential.py and cpp/heuristic.cpp. I also ran three short niced scratch measurements, all under /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-ClaudeTesting2/e59cf40d-e496-56e7-a6ac-661eab3c04d1/scratchpad/critic_robber/: bench.py (cost), shadow.py and shadow2.py (a scratch copy of the R1 wrapper on 260 robber/knight decisions from 40 heuristic-bot self-play games), and shadow_main.py (260 main-phase decisions of knight holders).
critique_verdicts.verdict: R1's persistence term is the strongest idea, but the plan has fixable engineering and statistical defects. On the positive side, persistence is sound, leaves the C++ static_value untouched, costs about 1.15x (I measured roughly 192 leaves per decision and about 10 us of Python per leaf), and acts where claimed. In my scratch shadow it changed 69% of the robber decisions that hit a knight holder and almost nothing else. The defects: (1) as planned, R3's counted-mode game test would be silently inert, because determinization and evidence tracking run in the adapter, outside ParamBot's override scope. (2) R1 would mis-target in counted mode, where determinized states deal uniform dev cards with dev_known=True, and in the Colonist advisor, and the plan never tests it with hidden information. (3) The mechanism gates rely on action logs and an ablate.py hook that don't exist; ablate.py belongs to the SPSA/factorial agent. (4) The non-inferiority rule is a coin flip at 2,000 seeds, and the uncorrected interim looks should use league/sequential.py. (5) The insurance term rewards a knight holder for making itself the natural target (the target key includes hand size). (6) The proposed cache key is incomplete. (7) Two plug-in points touch C++-mirrored functions despite 'cpp_impact: None': steal_exposure_fast and expected_hidden_vp. Recommended order: a zero-game shadow; then persistence-only R1 in self-play, 3 x 800 games with O'Brien-Fleming boundaries and adapter or on_action counters; Stage C only on ADOPT and phrased as a harm screen; R2 gated by the shadow; R3 and R4 handed to the card-counting area with the adapter-option fix and exact posterior dealing. Land all flag-off code in one commit to keep default-arm reuse intact. The proof run executes from /home/user/proof_snapshot2, so repository edits cannot contaminate it. Process note: I ran two read-only git commands (log and status) before seeing the no-git rule. Nothing in the repository was changed; the scratch scripts are in the scratchpad's critic_robber/ folder.

design.area: Card counting uses: resource odds for Monopoly and the robber, and reading opponents' held development cards (hidden VP / secret leader, knight threat and robber kicks, Monopoly plausibility)
design.summary:
Revised after both critiques. I re-checked every disputed fact in the code and ran three short niced log parses.

Every code claim the critiques made holds:
- ParamBot applies overrides only inside reset/decide/observe/explain.
- _follow_tracker resyncs the counter when the tracker raises.
- catanatron_players.py is pure Catanatron (it imports nothing from catanbot).
- bench_catanatron uses CATANBOT="catanbot" as our seat's label.
- arm_key hashes a fixed key_ctx.
- CatanbotPlayer defaults to seed=0.
- Colonist turns start at a roll or a 'turn' event.
- The default depth-1 search values finished leaves statically.
- static_value prices a held card at 0.12.

One error of my own: tuning.overridden does not exist; the API is tuning.apply/restore.

The diagnosis is unchanged. Counting is not the Monopoly bottleneck; reading opponents' development cards is the gap; and none of it can be proven against Catanatron. The proof data now finished make that firmer: full T1/T2/T3/T10 won 59.5% (n=2,200), counted T7/T8/T9/T11 won 60.3% (n=2,160). The campaign row t2_counted_info@value is therefore redundant.

New calibration, on T1-T11 logs with a tracker-view card model:
- The old one-parameter hazard (0.5) fails an age-stratified gate on ValueFunction. Its log-loss for cards held 10+ turns is 1.85 vs 1.06 for uniform: Catanatron hoards Road Building.
- A per-type-present joint likelihood with a per-type floor (H=0.85, EPS=0.03) beats uniform in every opponent class and every age bucket.
- Hidden-VP mean squared error: ours 0.237 vs 0.829, ValueFunction 0.216 vs 0.435, AlphaBeta 0.089 vs 0.389, SameTurn 0.099 vs 0.468.

Revised plan, all off by default:
1. **devbelief.hazard**, rebuilt:
   - bookkeeping stores sufficient statistics, and hazards are applied lazily under the ParamBot overrides;
   - per-type-present likelihood with an EPS floor;
   - exact dynamic-programming sampling with history-aware no-win caps;
   - dealing that consumes the shared random stream exactly as the default does;
   - error isolation;
   - four tunables;
   - Python only, no C++ impact.
2. **advisor.dev_read**: the first adoption, with no game budget. It adds per-opponent card odds, a conditioned secret-leader alert and a Monopoly-threat forecast from the bank. It uses an unfitted human preset and logs card ages for later fitting.
3. **shadow.dev_oracle**: a zero-game three-arm shadow (uniform / hazard / true dev cards dealt) scored by paired value regret. It gates every game-level test.
4. **search.knight_kick**, a new consumer. A robbed victim holding a knight kicks the robber next turn 99.4% of the time. This is a depth-1 leaf chance node in exact evaluator units; the critique measured it and I re-ran it.
5. **harness.selfbot_opponents**: its contract bugs are fixed, and its games are gated on the shadow result.

search.mono_threat and devcards.mono_convert are SHELVED at design; their formulas are corrected in case they are revived.

The game-level non-inferiority run against ValueFunction becomes a 200-game smoke run. It can optionally ride a shared counted default arm after a code freeze.

features.name: Age- and behaviour-aware posterior over opponents' hidden dev cards (per-type-present likelihood, eps floor, exact DP sampling, history-aware no-win caps, RNG-neutral dealing)
features.description:
Replace uniform dealing of opponents' hidden dev cards in counted-mode (and advisor) determinizations with a posterior. It uses how long each card has been held without being played, given that a player may play one card per turn and that VP cards are never played.

The trackers keep only sufficient statistics per opponent, with no hazard values baked in:
- type-less card records (own-turn index of purchase);
- the player's own-turn history (whether a dev card was played, a knight-context flag, the Monopoly payoff, and the maximum public VP during the turn);
- coverage intervals of past plays per type.

Likelihoods are computed lazily inside determinize / dev_posterior under the candidate's overrides. So tuned values reach them, which fixes critique 2's A/A trap.

The likelihood is per type present, not per card: holding 2 knights does not make a no-play turn twice as unlikely (critique 1, measured). A floor EPS per type bounds how far a hoarded type can be ruled out (critique 2; measured to fix ValueFunction's Road Building hoarding).

Sampling is exact by dynamic programming (DP) over card records and pool counts. The no-win constraint lives inside the DP, including the history rule: a card held while its owner stood at vps_to_win-1 public VP on his own turn is not a VP card. The tables are cached per tracker version, so the 4 determinizations of a decision share them.

Dealing is RNG-neutral: the existing uniform deal always runs on the shared rng. When the model is informative, only the dev hands are overwritten from a side stream copied from the pre-deal rng state. Hands, search seeds and deck order therefore stay common to both arms.

All consumers pick this up automatically because they read dev_known determinized states: hidden VP in static_value, threat and danger (secret leader); knights in steal_exposure_fast (knight threat); the deck's VP share (our dev-buy value); knight_kick; and Monopoly holdings.
features.formulas:
Bookkeeping per opponent j (O(1) per event, no RNG, isolated by try/except):
- recs_j: purchase own-turn index b for each hidden unplayed card.
- turns_j: for each own turn tau, the fields noplay_tau, kctx_tau, pay_tau, maxpub_tau (defined below).
- cov_j[t]: intervals (b', tau').

Turn fields:
- noplay_tau = 1 when j played no dev card in tau. A per-player flag 'played since my last turn end' is set by on_play and cleared by on_turn_end, so ordering does not matter.
- kctx_tau = 1 when, at j's first entry of tau (ROLL or a pre-roll PLAY_KNIGHT), the robber hex touches a j building, or a knight would give j Largest Army (j.played_K + 1 >= 3 and greater than every other player's played knights).
- pay_tau = max_r sum_{k != j} E[hand_k[r]] (human preset only).
- maxpub_tau = the maximum public VP of j during tau.

On a play of type t in tau': remove the youngest eligible record b' and append (b', tau') to cov_j[t].

Eligibility: record r is eligible in turn tau when tau > b_r (official rules / 3.3), or tau >= b_r (3.2.1, where new_devs_unplayable is False).

Aging set for record r if assigned type t: S_t(r) = {tau : noplay_tau, r eligible at tau, and tau not inside any (b', tau') of cov_j[t]}. The played card of type t explains those turns.

Player likelihood of an assignment A_j: L_j(A_j) = prod over non-VP types t present in A_j of F_t, with F_t = (1 - EPS) * prod_{tau in S_t(r_t)} (1 - h_t(tau)) + EPS, where r_t is the oldest record assigned t. VP cards have factor 1.

Bot preset hazards: h_t = H (0.85) for every non-VP type; h_K(tau) = H_KNIGHT_CTX when kctx_tau (default equal to H, i.e. inactive).

Win caps: sort records oldest first r_1..r_m. cap_k = V - 1 - max(maxpub_tau for tau >= b_{r_k}), and for k = m also V - 1 - public_now_j. Require #VP(r_1..r_k) <= cap_k.

Joint prior from dealing uniformly from pool pi (PublicBelief.dev_pool): P(A) is proportional to prod_t fall(pi_t, sum_j n_{j,t}) * prod_j L_j(A_j) * caps, where fall(x, n) = x(x-1)...(x-n+1).

Exact sampling:
1. Per player j, a forward DP over records (state = mask of non-VP types present, count vector n_j) gives W_j(n_j), pruned by the caps.
2. Across players, a forward convolution over the used vector u: Z_j(u) = sum_{n_j} Z_{j-1}(u - n_j) * W_j(n_j) * prod_t fall(pi_t - (u - n_j)_t, n_{j,t}).
3. Sample backward: n_J, ..., n_1; then each player's record types from its stored DP.
4. deck = pi - sum_j n_j. Cards bought this turn by the current player go to dev_cards_new (VP stays in dev_cards), as in the existing split.

The tables are cached per (tracker event count, devbelief tunable values). A guard over a table budget of 200k entries falls back to uniform and counts devbelief_fallbacks.

RNG neutrality:
- st = rng.getstate(); run the existing _deal_devs on rng unchanged.
- If ENABLED and some unknown holder has a record with a non-empty aging set or a binding cap, then side = Random(); side.setstate(st); overwrite dev_cards, dev_cards_new, dev_count and dev_deck of the unknown holders from the DP sample drawn with side.

Posterior outputs by forward-backward: P_r(t) per record; P(hidden VP_j = k) exactly, under the caps.

features.expected_effect:
Belief effect, measured on held-out logs with the tracker-view record model (H=0.85, EPS=0.03):
- Hidden-VP mean squared error: our-bot-like -71% (0.829 to 0.237); ValueFunction -50%; AlphaBeta -77%; SameTurn -79%.
- Log-loss for P(at least 1 VP) falls from 0.86-1.04 to 0.30-0.59, and is better than uniform in every age bucket.

- About 1-3 of our turns per game at a dev-heavy table (robber target, knight timing, trade refusal to the secret leader, dev buys, since fewer VP are left in the deck).
- About 0.2 per game against ValueFunction.

Win rate: against Catanatron, about 0 (the counted-vs-full gap is about 0: 60.3% vs 59.5%). At dev-heavy or human tables my guess is +0.5 to +2 pp. The shadow (feature 3) replaces that guess with a measured regret.
features.how_to_test:
(A) Calibration gate. It drives the real DevAgeModel through PublicInfoTracker replays of the T1-T11 logs, so the implementation and the calibration are checked in one run (about 10 CPU-min niced).

Pass requires all of:
- hidden-VP mean squared error at least 30% below uniform in every opponent class;
- log-loss no worse than uniform in every class x age bucket (1, 2, 3-5, 6-9, 10+);
- devbelief_errors = 0 and devbelief_fallbacks under 0.1%.

The scratch implementation already passes with H=0.85, EPS=0.03. It also reports the per-card-floor variant for comparison, and the knight-context stratum.

(B) The shadow in feature shadow.dev_oracle.

(C) No-harm smoke: scripts/ablate_catanatron.py --tunable devbelief.ENABLED --values 1 --opponent value --info counted --seeds 100 (200 games, about 15 min on 1 core).
- Checks: crashes, decision-time ratio at most 1.05, replay --check, devbelief_errors = 0.
- Reports the fraction of discordant seeds, which is low thanks to RNG-neutral dealing.
- The 4,000-game non-inferiority run is dropped as a standalone test: it was an effective A/A run.
- Optional: it rides a shared counted default arm in the post-freeze counted batch (2,000 seeds; non-inferiority margin about 2 pp thanks to the common random numbers).

(D) Game superiority test at the selfbot table only if (B) implies at least 4 pp. Otherwise it is SHELVED by pre-registration.

Adoption as the counted-mode default: A + B pass + C clean, with the user's OK (belief-evidence policy).

features.name: Zero-game dev-reading shadow: uniform vs hazard vs true-dev-cards arms, paired value regret, plus the reveal_devs oracle flag
features.description:
Measures, without playing games, how much our decisions lose from not knowing opponents' dev cards (the headroom) and how much the hazard posterior recovers.

It replays positions of a catanbot seat from proof logs through PublicInfoTracker and decides each one three ways. The arms share the same hand samples and search rng, which RNG-neutral dealing makes possible:
- U: uniform dev deal;
- H: hazard deal;
- O: the true opponent dev cards dealt, via a harness-only tracker flag reveal_devs (buys are public, steals and discards stay hidden).

So a disagreement can come only from dev dealing. This is critique 1's oracle fix, and it avoids full information, which also reveals the resource hands.

Scoring is by paired value regret under the oracle's own counted evaluation (critique 2): continuous, and far more powerful than a sign test on agreement. The shadow gates every game-level card-reading test, and it also gives knight_kick's counted-mode consumer a check.
features.formulas:
Positions: about 2,000 searched decisions of a catanbot seat in T4 logs (later the selfbot-table logs). Enriched with:
- every position where some opponent holds a record with at least 2 no-play eligible turns;
- all BUY_DEVELOPMENT_CARD, MOVE_ROBBER / PLAY_KNIGHT and trade-response decisions.

Arms X in {U, H}: K=4 determinizations. The shared rng gives identical hand samples (counter.sample first, RNG-neutral dealing); a_X is the adapter's aggregated choice.

Reference: V_O(a) = the mean over K_ref = 8 oracle determinizations (true opponent devs; hands from a separate fixed stream) of the searched value of a. Force-evaluate with legal = [a], so every chosen action gets a value in win-probability units.

regret_X = max_{a in {a_U, a_H, a_O}} V_O(a) - V_O(a_X).

Saving compute: run O and V_O only where a_U != a_H, plus a random 25% subsample for the headroom estimate.

Statistics:
- Headroom = E[regret_U].
- Captured = E[regret_U - regret_H], by paired t-test, reported per decision type.
- Decision-change rate = P(a_U != a_H) per searched decision.
- Implied game effect = captured x the mean number of searched decisions per game (from the result files). It is evaluator-based, hence optimistic; used only for gating.

Pre-registered rules:
- Change rate below 1% at the T4 table: the bot change is advisor-only.
- Captured > 0 at p < 0.05: (B) passes.
- Implied effect of at least 4 pp at a 3-dev-heavy table (T4 rate x 3): queue test (D) on the selfbot table. Otherwise SHELVE game tests for dev reading.

features.name: Knight-kick leaf chance node: a robber block on a knight holder lasts until that player's turn
features.description:
At the default depth 1, a finished leaf where the robber sits on an opponent's hex is valued by static_value as a lasting 0.55*pv production loss for that opponent. A victim that holds a playable knight kicks the robber on its next turn with probability 0.99 (T1+T4), usually onto someone else, often us.

This feature turns such leaves into an exact chance node in the evaluator's own units: with probability KICK the first knight-holding blocked opponent in turn order moves the robber by its own robber policy and spends the knight (Largest Army updated). So the search stops paying for blocks that will not last. It also sees retaliation and the victim's Largest Army progress.

In full information the knights are known. In counted mode they come from the determinization, so devbelief feeds it directly. It fires on about 15% of robberies at dev-heavy tables and about 1% against Catanatron.

It uses a generic 'leaf chance events' hook that a revived mono_threat could reuse. This is the most decision-relevant consumer of the dev posterior (critique 1's missing idea). It touches the robber area's subject, so it must be coordinated with that agent.
features.formulas:
Applies only when cfg.depth == 1 and cfg.kick > 0, to finished leaves s (s.current != me, not game over):
- h = s.robber; V = players != me with a building on h, in turn order after me.
- j* = the first j in V with dev_cards[K] + dev_cards_new[K] >= 1 (dev_known). If none, the leaf is unchanged.
- Kick target (h', v') = robber.best_robber_move(root state with the robber moved to h, j*) — no politics or model weights, like _greedy_turn with them off — cached per (h, j*) per search.
- s' = s.copy(): robber = h'; j*'s knight consumed (dev_cards first, then dev_cards_new); played_knights[j*] += 1; engine._update_largest_army(s', j*). The steal is ignored (documented).
- value(s) = (1 - KICK) * v(s) + KICK * v(s'), where v = Searcher._eval (whichever evaluator, including PathsEvaluator). So the units are exact and there is no weight to tune.
- The extra states of one expansion level are evaluated in one batched _eval call.
- At depth >= 2 it is off: the simulated opponent turns already play knights, and native futures bypass Python.
plug_in_points: catanbot/search.py: SearchConfig.kick (float, default 0.0); in search(), after the finished nodes of a level are evaluated, apply the leaf chance correction to them (a generic _leaf_chance hook)
catanbot/knightkick.py (new; not robber.py, which belongs to the robber area): kick_state(s, j, target) and the (h, j) cache; imports robber.best_robber_move and engine._update_largest_army read-only

catanbot/tuning.py: search-kind tunable search.kick (candidates 0.95)
catanbot/tuning.py:play_paired_game: a generic per-seat event-counter hook, coordinated with the factorial/tune_joint agent rather than a knight-specific branch (mechanism metrics)
features.off_switch: search.kick is a search-kind tunable, default 0.0: no correction and bit-identical values. Candidate 0.95. Spec key kick. Depth-1 only.
features.cpp_impact: None. It is a Python search-layer mixture of evaluator outputs on extra states. The evaluator (C++ or not), static_value and placement are untouched, and no needs_python_evaluator is needed. Native futures (depth >= 2) are unaffected because the feature is off there.
features.cost: About 1.00x when no blocked knight holder exists (a one-line check per finished leaf). In affected positions (the robber on a knight holder, about 10-20% of positions at dev-heavy tables) it costs one state copy and one batched evaluation per finished leaf, plus one cached best_robber_move per distinct robber hex: about 1.03-1.08x there, about 1.01x overall.
features.expected_effect: At self-play tables, about 15% of our robberies hit a knight holder today. I expect that share to fall toward 5-8%, with longer blocks and fewer retaliations. Decisions changed: about 0.1-0.3 robber placements per game per seat. Win rate: +0.2 to +0.8 pp at dev-heavy tables (my guess), about 0 against Catanatron (1.1% of robberies). The win rate is unprovable at 2,400 games (MDE about 3.3 pp), so the mechanism is the stop rule.
features.how_to_test:
Self-play, full information (knights known), run as one cell of the other agent's self-play factorial batch with a shared default arm (not standalone).

Mechanism metrics, paired, pre-registered:
- the share of our robber placements that land on a knight holder (expected drop of 7 or more pp; SE about 1.5 pp at 600 games);
- the mean number of opponent rolls our placed robber survives;
- the rate at which the robber is placed on us within one turn of our robbery.

Interim look at 600 games: stop (put on ice) if the knight-holder share has not dropped by at least 3 pp. Otherwise complete 2,400 games; the win rate is a secondary metric, expected INCONCLUSIVE.

Counted mode: add knight-kick decisions to the shadow's position set as a sanity check. No Catanatron run (it would be about an A/A run).
tests_to_write: kick=0: search values are bit-identical to the base on random states and at depth 2
A single knight-holding victim: the leaf value equals (1-KICK) v(s) + KICK v(s'), with v(s') from a hand-built state
No knight holder on the robber hex: unchanged, and no extra evaluation
The kick that gives j* Largest Army updates the VP in s'
Composes with paths=1 (the mixture of PathsEvaluator outputs); the cache is keyed by (h, j*) and reset per search
Counted mode: a determinization with a dealt knight triggers the correction
features.moderate_fallback: Hand it to the robber-area agent as a prior-level tweak: in best_robber_move's hex score, scale the block-damage part by (1 - KICK * 1[the blocked player holds a playable knight]). It is cheaper, but priors only order expansion, so the expected effect is smaller.

features.name: Dev-heavy hidden-information table: our default bot as the three opponents in the Catanatron harness (games gated on the shadow)
features.formulas:
Game batch, only if (B) implies at least 4 pp: a shared default arm (our seat counted-uniform) and the candidate hazard arm (devbelief.ENABLED=1). Optionally an oracle arm (reveal_devs=1) when the shadow's ceiling is ambiguous. 2,000 paired seeds per arm; se = sd of per-seed differences / sqrt(n); MDE80 = 2.8 se, about 4 pp.

Decision rules, with no dead zone:
- hazard vs uniform significant and positive: adopt;
- not significant: game INCONCLUSIVE, and adoption rests on A+B+C (user policy);
- significantly negative: reject.

If the oracle arm runs: oracle - uniform not significant means SHELVE all dev-reading game tests.

Cost comes from a 20-game niced pilot, with the opponents' decision time reported separately. Extrapolation: 7-12 s per game.

features.name: Opponent Monopoly threat (SHELVED at design)
features.description:
Shelved, following both critiques:
- The old Delta was mis-scaled 4-8x against static_value (about 0.85-1.4 points per threatened card vs 0.12 per held card and 0.25*cv for robber exposure), which would push the bot into 4:1 dumps.
- The only setting where it is measurable (full-information self-play) does not transfer: hidden Monopolies are rare (2/25 of the pool) and are played at once.
- The expected effect (0.1-0.3 pp) cannot be proven.

If ever revived, it should be the exact leaf chance node below, sharing knight_kick's _leaf_chance hook.
features.formulas:
Depth 1, finished leaf s. For each opponent j holding a Monopoly (dev_known):
- P_j = 0.85 (the bots' play rate).
- The top-2 targets by q_j(r), proportional to payoff_j(r) * (1 + need_j(r)), renormalised.
- value = (1 - P_j) v(s) + P_j sum_{r in top2} q_j(r) v(s after j monopolizes r), where v is the evaluator via _eval. That gives exact units, includes j's gain and needs no weight W.
plug_in_points: catanbot/search.py _leaf_chance hook (shared with knight_kick)
catanbot/devcards.py or a new catanbot/mono_threat.py (not robber.py)
catanbot/selfplay.py:make_bot spec key mono=
features.off_switch: search.mono_threat, search-kind, default 0.0 (not registered until revived).
features.cpp_impact: None (a Python mixture of evaluator outputs).
features.cost: Up to 2 extra evaluations per finished leaf when a Monopoly is held (about 1.02x).
features.expected_effect: About 0.2-0.4 cards per game saved in full-information self-play (dodging by building, not by 4:1 trades), about +0.1-0.3 pp. About 0 in hidden-information play.
features.how_to_test: Not queued. If revived: one cell of a self-play factorial with a 600-game mechanism look. Metric: cards lost to Monopoly per game (SE about 0.1), with guard metrics of 4:1 bank trades per game and total cards traded away. Put it on ice unless the loss falls and the 4:1 trades do not rise.
tests_to_write: The chance-node value equals a hand-computed mixture on a fixture

features.name: Monopoly resource by conversion value (SHELVED at design; formula corrected)
features.description: Counting is already sufficient for our own Monopoly choice (T7 equals T1). The remaining valuation headroom is about 0.3 build units per game, which cannot be proven. This entry is kept only for the corrected formula, and so its advisor fallback can be part of dev_card_advice.
features.formulas:
take_r = sum_{k != me} E[hand_k[r]]; P(take_r >= m) = sum over the counter's hypotheses w x 1[sum_k hyp_k[r] >= m].

V_r = the best value of up to 2 builds affordable from hand + take_r with port and bank ratios, minus the expected discard loss: E_loss = P7 x floor(L / 2) x rho x 1[L > 7], with P7 = 1 - (5/6)^4 = 0.518 (3 opponents' rolls and our own roll come before we can build again) and rho = 0.65 build units per card (settlement 2.8 / 4 cards, city 3.2 / 5).

r* = argmax V_r.

features.cpp_impact: None (Python priors and devcards).
features.cost: Under 1.01x (about 0.44 Monopoly decisions per game).
features.expected_effect: At most about +0.5 pp; about 0.1 decisions changed per game. Unprovable at 2,000 seeds.
features.how_to_test: Not queued. If bundled: a mechanism metric (the chosen resource's conversion value per Monopoly, paired), put on ice below +0.3 build units per play.

risks: The whole area is unprovable at game level against Catanatron: the counted-vs-full gap is about 0 (60.3% vs 59.5%, pooled over 4 opponent sets). Even at a dev-heavy table the implied effects are likely below the 4 pp MDE. Adoption must rest on calibration (A), the shadow (B) and a smoke run (C), which is a policy call for the user. The shadow's implied effect is evaluator-based and optimistic.

Bot-fitted hazards versus humans. H=0.85 with EPS=0.03 is calibrated on bots only. Humans hold knights (robber defence, Largest Army timing) and Monopoly (waiting for a payoff) longer. The bot preset would over-read human hoarders as VP holders, and so deal them too few knights, understating the knight threat and the knight kick. That is why the advisor uses the separate HUMAN preset and the counted-mode bot preset must not be used for human play until fitted on logged sessions.

Structure choice. The per-type-present likelihood (behaviourally right; critique 1's multi.py) is worse calibrated than a per-card floor on our-bot-like multi-card old holders: mean squared error at age 10+ is 0.343 vs 0.124. The per-type EPS floor gives multi-knight hoards more mass than bots warrant. Gate (A) compares both, and the choice is an implementation-time decision.
MAP record removal (the youngest eligible record) approximates the exact mixture over which card was played. The coverage intervals inherit that approximation.

Plumbing and silent A/A runs:
- Hazard values must be applied lazily under the override wrap, or candidate arms equal the default.
- Bookkeeping exceptions must never reach tracker.resync, or the default bot changes.
Both are covered by explicit tests.

RNG neutrality holds only if the whole overwrite (hands of unknown holders, the dev_cards_new split, the deck) uses the side stream. Any stray use of the shared rng breaks the common random numbers of the shadow and the smoke pairing.

Scheduling. code_fingerprint covers the whole package, so landing these off-by-default edits after campaign default arms are played forces those arms to be replayed. Land P1, P3 and P5 (and the other areas' flags) before the batch's code freeze, and share one counted default arm.

knight_kick overlaps the robber area and shares search.py with winpaths and the factorial work. Its mechanism counters need a generic per-seat event hook in tuning.play_paired_game, which the other agent also touches, so it must be coordinated.
The selfbot table's opponents see our full hand and do not trade. That is fair between arms, but it is not a Colonist game.
Our bot's tell: it holds only VP cards beyond 1 turn, so a human counter reads them with P above 0.95. The counter-measure is human-facing (politics rule).
Measurements share CPU with the running proof. Everything in this revision was niced and each run took under 60 s CPU. The scratch scripts are outside the repository.

critique_verdicts.lens: Catan strategy and correctness: rules, how strong human players use these mechanics, the user's intent, and whether each formula's size fits the static-value scale (10 points per VP). I checked the claims against catanbot/public_belief.py, counting.py, devcards.py, heuristic.py, robber.py, search.py, bench/public_info.py, bench/catanatron_adapter.py, colonist_log.py and agents/param_bot.py. I also ran two short niced log parses of proof T1+T4 (scratch scripts in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-ClaudeTesting2/e59cf40d-e496-56e7-a6ac-661eab3c04d1/scratchpad/critic/: multi.py, kick.py, retal.py).
critique_verdicts.verdict:
The diagnosis holds up. Counting is not the Monopoly bottleneck, reading dev cards is the real gap, and Catanatron can't measure any of it. I checked the plumbing claims against the code and they are correct: counted mode searches determinized dev_known states; ParamBot does not wrap the adapter's determinize; counting.dev_pool subtracts only played knights; nothing models an opponent's Monopoly threat.

- **P1 (devbelief)** is the right core but is not yet correct. The per-card likelihood must become a per-type-present likelihood; the logs show a second knight barely changes the play rate. H_CAP must be replaced by a real likelihood floor or a mixture, because the bot-fitted constants would misread human knight hoarders and Monopoly waiters as secret leaders. Keep it minimal (one hazard plus the knight context) and give the advisor a separate human preset.
- **Tests for P1:** drop the uninformative non-inferiority run against ValueFunction. Fix the shadow test's oracle and rng coupling.
- **P2 (harness)** is worth building, but only with a dev-oracle arm and a decision rule that has no dead zone.
- **P3 (mono_threat)** is mis-scaled by roughly 4-8x against static_value (about 1 point per card vs 0.12 for a held card and 0.25 for a stolen one). It would push the bot into more 4:1 dumps and cannot be proven at the budget, so shelve it or cut it to a priors-only mechanism screen.
- **P4 (mono_convert)** is correctly shelved. Its discard term is also mis-scaled.

The most valuable missing piece is robber block duration from knight holdings: a robbed knight holder kicks the robber next turn with probability 0.99.

critique_verdicts.lens: Engineering and testability: default-bot byte identity, whether the plug-in points are real (checked against the code), C++ parity and search cost, whether each test can detect its effect within 2,000 paired seeds or about 2,400 self-play games, test coverage, and file conflicts with the other areas.
critique_verdicts.verdict:
P1 is sound in its core and its main plug-in is real. PublicBelief._deal_devs deals opponents' cards, and determinized states carry dev_known=True, which both the C++ static_value and steal_exposure_fast read exactly. So there is no C++ change and no needs_python_evaluator; this checks out in the code. But four engineering defects must be fixed first:
1. Hazard constants would be baked in at bookkeeping time, outside ParamBot scope, so tuned values never reach aging.
2. The always-on bookkeeping can change the default bot through tracker.resync if it ever raises.
3. H_CAP does not stop over-confidence. My T1 log count shows ValueFunction's old cards plateau at about 72% VP and 27% Road Building, so an eps mixture floor and age-stratified gates are needed.
4. The shadow test (B) needs common random numbers (RNG-neutral dealing) and a regret metric to have real power.

P2 is the right idea, but its moderate fallback is invalid (the two candidate seats cancel out). Its decision rule leaves 2-4 pp undefined, and (D) is underpowered by construction. A dev-oracle shadow arm should gate it. Its plug-ins must also respect the purity of catanatron_players.py, the CATANBOT label, and arm-key stability for --reuse.

P3 should be shelved at design, like P4. Its only measurable setting (full-information self-play) does not transfer to hidden-information play. Its Delta is mis-scaled against static_value's card values, which invites 4:1 dumping. And its 'exact' composition claims fail for PathsEvaluator and native depth 2 or more.

Proof data finished since the design was written (T8, T9) shows counted play at or above full information against Catanatron (pooled 59.9% vs 59.1%), so the queued t2_counted_info row is redundant.
